speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, overall, we have made progress, but we still need to go further.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we will press ahead with our work on industry transformation and we also hope to see more companies making full use of the schemes available to restructure and transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even as we press on with productivity improvements, we also have to gear up for the green transition and the decarbonisation of our economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And several Members, including Ms Carrie Tan, Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Prof Koh Lian Pin spoke passionately about this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many of these moves are a work in progress, and the Minister for Trade and Industry will be happy to share more, I am sure, at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Derrick Goh and Mr Don Wee also shared that the application process for grants is sometimes cumbersome for SMEs and disbursements can take a long time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our economic agencies will continue to work closely with companies to support them through the different stages of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In processing applications and claims, we strive to be as efficient as possible, while ensuring accountability and safeguarding the integrity of the system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I hope Members understand this need to balance speed with the need for accountability in the use of public monies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will look into your suggestions and our agencies will continue to streamline and improve processes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we grow the economy, we will also ensure that the growth translates into better jobs and opportunities for our workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a dynamic and vibrant economy, we must expect a continual refreshing and updating of jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unproductive jobs will become obsolete, and new, better, more productive roles will be created in their place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These new jobs could be within the same companies and sectors as where the unproductive jobs are eliminated.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They could also be offered by more successful and expanding employers in the same sector, or in other sectors altogether that grow to take the place of the declining ones.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This churn is an integral part of healthy economic growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it does create uncertainties for workers, because workers will need to reskill and upskill to stay relevant and take on new roles, be it in the same company, or in a different company, or even in a different industry altogether.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are investing significantly in skills and human capital, to help our workers progress in their careers and earn better wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We started this journey – in fact, it has been an ongoing journey, but we made a further push with the SkillsFuture movement in 2015 and we have made progress since then.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the individual level, through SkillsFuture, we have empowered individuals to take charge of their own skills development and created a culture of lifelong learning, which is growing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Amongst our institutes of higher learning (IHLs), we have brought about a major mindset and paradigm change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our universities, polytechnics and ITE no longer just focus on pre-employment training, but they are now firmly embedded in the continuing education and training space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the employer level, we have also made progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the past, when you asked employers about the competencies and skills that their workers need, you probably might not get a clear response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through efforts like NTUC's Company Training Committees, employers and unions are coming together to focus on job redesign and training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Yesterday, many Labour Members of Parliament spoke passionately about this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And you can hear from the speeches that we have come a long way, but we will do more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Actually, the role that the integrator plays is not new.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have always recognised the need for such an entity – it could be a training provider, a company or an industry association – but there is always a need for such an entity to act as a coordinator and bring together the various stakeholders in a particular sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Up to now, this integrator role has been done in, perhaps, a more ad hoc fashion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We hope that with additional Government resourcing for this new formalised role and very clear outcome indicators and KPIs, we can achieve better quality training and job matches.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I appreciate the strong interest in the Jobs-Skills Integrators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are only at the start of this initiative and there is still much more to be done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Education will share more at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Members – Mr Patrick Tay, Ms Mariam Jaafar and Assoc Prof Lim – also spoke about the challenges that mature workers will face especially if they are displaced or retrenched, and I agree with them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Younger workers in their 20s will often be able to get back to work quickly, particularly in the current tight labour market, where there are still high vacancy rates and job openings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But if you are in your 40s and 50s, and are displaced or retrenched, it is harder to find a job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At that age, many will also have heavier family responsibilities, to their young children, ageing parents, or both.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, they find it difficult to go for more extensive training, especially to switch to a new growth area.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I hope Members appreciate that we have to think through and design these moves carefully.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have to ensure that whatever we do does not erode the incentive to work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to provide some cushion while the workers undertake training to upgrade their skills and take on new roles that better fit their abilities and aptitudes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And when workers across the whole economy find their work meaningful, the result will be higher job satisfaction, greater fulfilment and a boost to productivity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Members in this House, I am sure, will remember that it was not so long ago when the Government was being criticised for pursuing a "growth at all costs" strategy – that we were chasing economic growth at the expense of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I think Ms Carrie Tan and Ms Nadia Samdin, to some extent, echoed some of these sentiments in their speeches, when they talked about adopting different models of success that are not just driven by a single-minded pursuit of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, now that growth is slower, we are in a different situation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members in this House now are concerned that we are not sufficiently focused on growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That if we are faced with a shrinking pie, contentious disputes over how to distribute limited resources will be inevitable, which can be very socially divisive, as we have seen in many other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But Sir, in fact, we have always taken a balanced approach in our economic development and strategies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our focus has always been to grow the economy, not for its own sake, but as a means to improving the well-being and lives of everyone in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In all that we do, we work closely with our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As Senior Minister of State Heng Chee How, Minister of State Desmond Tan, the Labour Members of Parliament and Mr Raj Joshua Thomas highlighted, tripartism is the competitive advantage that sets Singapore apart and distinguishes us from other countries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our model of tripartism has been the bedrock for Singapore's growth and prosperity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it has been critical in enabling us to rebuild from crises and to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in Singapore, it is not about "pro-business" versus "pro-workers"; neither is it about "pro-growth" versus "pro-redistribution".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about all of us – employers, unions and the Government – coming together, working together to advance the well-being of Singaporeans and build a better future for ourselves and our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The third broad bucket of issues is about whether we are doing enough to help Singaporeans and households in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And indeed, many Members spoke up in this area and supported the Government's efforts to help Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we have provided comprehensive measures to help Singaporeans cope with higher prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the help extends to sandwiched and middle-income families too, like those whom Mr Xie Yao Quan, Mr Abdul Samad and Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman were concerned about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I am also heartened by the efforts of the Consumers Association of Singapore like Price Kaki which Mr Melvin Yong spoke about and we will consider and look into his suggestions as well, and the fact that companies like NTUC FairPrice and Sheng Siong are doing their part to help cushion the impact of higher prices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another topic that many Members spoke about is on housing affordability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We debated this at length earlier this month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I was not going to touch on it originally but since so many of you spoke about this, I thought I should cover it briefly in my remarks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are all concerned about the affordability and accessibility of public housing in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I think it is important we understand the underlying causes for the challenges we face today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because failure to diagnose the problem properly can lead to the wrong solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Desmond Lee is in the hot seat now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I was in the hot seat then for a different reason.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And at that time, we used the same methodology to price Build-To-Order (BTO) flats then, as we are doing now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But when resale prices were falling, no one seemed to be unduly concerned about the prices of new flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the contrary, there was a great anxiety that there would be a huge overhang of flats and we would end up with a price meltdown.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is precisely why the Workers' Party proposed in 2019 to cut back the annual BTO supply to just 9,000 flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I read the letter published in The Straits Times today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Workers' Party now says that it was not a proposal.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it was quite clear in the Working Paper in a section headlined "Calibrating the construction of new BTO estates"; it says very clearly that "around 9,000 or so dwelling units are required annually" based on various population parameters, otherwise HDB will have a vacancy rate problem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Then how did the situation change so quickly in the last three years?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had a pandemic that disrupted our BTO building programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And when that supply was disrupted and waiting times became longer, people felt anxious and more started applying for BTO flats earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Others decided to get a resale flat instead because waiting time was so long; so that drives up resale demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we had a confluence of both delayed project delivery and increased demand, contributing to the situation that we are in now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Who could have anticipated and predicted all this?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, if we had adopted the WP proposal – well, never mind, heeded their advice since you do not want to call it a proposal – and if we had done so and cut back the building of new flats and adopted their subsequent proposal to allow singles aged below 35 to buy new flats, we would be facing a much bigger supply-demand imbalance today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, you know, let us all show some humility in this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What happened could not have been predicted and let us refrain from passing judgment with the benefit of hindsight.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under the current circumstances, the WP now says that the house price-to-income ratio should be lowered to three.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Why not make it two, or even one?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Regardless of the number, more funding will be required to make new flats cheaper.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, I think, the WP does not want to talk about increasing subsidies and making the taxpayer cough out more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, they have chosen instead to go with what they think is probably a more expedient and seemingly painless option – which is to dip into the reserves by selling the state land to HDB at a lower cost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we must remember public housing land is sold directly to HDB at a fair market value determined by the Chief Valuer (CV) using established and accepted valuation principles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What would be the basis for the Government to get the CV to change the valuation method?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Pritam Singh alluded to, in his question, that there is a discrepancy because State Land sold under the Government Land Sales (GLS) programme can potentially enjoy a 15% discount.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fair market value of State Land sold through an open tender, such as under the GLS programme, is determined through price discovery when developers bid for the land.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But that is a reserve price, not a discount.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And this reserve price serves as a guidepost for the Government to assess the bids that are received before awarding the tender.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, if the highest tendered price is below this 85% threshold, we might want to check this against other factors like the prevailing market conditions, the number of independent bids received and the specific circumstances about the site.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, it is a guidepost for us to do our checks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if we are convinced that the bids are competitive and reflect actual market conditions because it went through a tender process, then we would still proceed with the highest acceptable bid in the tender because that is the fair market value of the land.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Public housing land is not sold through an open tender like the GLS programme because there is only one developer – the HDB.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But HDB flats are purchased and sold all the time in the open market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is a well-established open market value for the flats, and therefore working backwards, one can calculate the value of the land used to build HDB flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These transactions provide the CV with up-to-date market data to consider when making his or her independent determination of the fair market value of public housing land.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These valuations are based on objective facts; they are not an arbitrary subjective opinion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also real, as every HDB homeowner knows who has sold his flat for more than he paid HDB, and used the capital gain to upgrade to a bigger flat, or to put aside for their retirement needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And if you were to try to artificially "reset" the housing market in this manner, you will risk destabilising the entire property market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Actually, Assoc Prof Lim recognised this in his Facebook post two days ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He said that with the proposal by the Workers' Party to reduce the land price, some homeowners who have bought their flats under current terms and subsequently wish to sell their flat for various reasons, quote, "may go underwater" or, quote, "have to stomach a loss".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Is that what the Workers' Party wants to do – to arbitrarily wipe out a significant chunk of the value of Singaporeans' hard-earned properties?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But at least Assoc Prof Lim acknowledged this problem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because Mr Leong Mun Wai, who similarly wants HDB BTO prices to be drastically reduced, has claimed that his proposal has no impact on the resale market and Singaporeans can have their cake and eat it too – cheap BTO prices, high resale prices, home buyers still enjoying enormous capital gains, and the Government does not have to do anything.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It seems like magic, but it is really a raid on the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Suffice to say, there are no magic solutions to solve the current housing issues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government's approach – and what we believe is the right thing to do – is to tackle the root cause of the problem.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, let us ramp up BTO supply; catch up with the delays that had arisen over the COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: HDB is doing the best it can, and Ministry of Finance (MOF) is supporting them with the resources to do so and I am confident that we will, through all these efforts, get things back on track soon.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is also a view being put out by some Members – I think, Ms Hazel Poa and others highlighted – that the Government's policy on land value is driving up public housing prices, that leads to continued increases in subsidies for BTO flats, which may not be sustainable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But now, again, we are looking at this now and the concern arises because of the current cyclical tightness in the public housing market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The situation will be different once the market stabilises or if you have a down market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, rather than look at the ups and downs, cyclically, the fact is land value will ultimately be based on economic fundamentals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, because it will take time for the supply to go up, we have made some moves in this Budget to manage demand.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know quite a number of Members have highlighted concerns that this increased grant will cause sellers to ask for higher resale prices and may not work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And in fact, there will always be a risk like this when we increase the grants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why we considered it very carefully, and we took into account the property cooling measures we had implemented and HDB’s progress in ramping up the BTO supply, before we decided on this move.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Furthermore, not all flat buyers will benefit from the increased grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, while the enhanced grant may have some impact on resale prices, overall first-timers should benefit from the grant and pay less when they buy a resale flat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is a targeted support measure, rather than a broad-based move; and we are confident that it will help first-timer families and singles buying in the resale market, and indirectly also reduce some of the demand for BTO flats.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is certainly a lot more we can cover on housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not a housing debate: it is a Budget debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I have focused on the key points, especially where it relates to land and reserves matters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I am sure there will be more to discuss, and the Minister for National Development will address them at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members including Dr Wan Rizal, Mr Desmond Choo, Mr Leon Perera, and Mr Christopher de Souza also spoke about what more we can do to tackle the related issues of inequality and social mobility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As I highlighted in the Budget Statement, our moves to uplift lower-wage workers through Workfare and Progressive Wages are showing results.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the past five years, our lower-wage workers have consistently seen higher income growth than those at the median.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will continue with our efforts to uplift the incomes of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last September, we expanded the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) to workers in the retail sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In July, we will cover workers in waste management.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, our Progressive Wage approach covers the vast majority of lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the moves we are making will have a positive impact in uplifting their salaries over the coming years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond these PWM sectors, we are charting out skills-based career ladders for tradesmen in key essential services like plumbers, electricians and aircon mechanics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Earlier this month, the Labour Movement mooted the Career Progression Model, a new framework which will uplift the work prospects and wages of skilled essential tradesmen and professionalise these trades.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will support the Labour Movement in these efforts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also focusing on new entrants to the workforce, especially our ITE graduates, which Mr Desmond Choo and others spoke about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are equipping them with industry-relevant skills and a strong foundation for future learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are positive indications and we will continue to do more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will do our part, but we will not be able to narrow wage gaps on our own.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As many Members highlighted, to ensure sustainable growth in real wages for our lower-wage workers, Singaporeans need to chip in too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As consumers, all of us must be prepared to pay more for services delivered by our fellow Singaporeans, be it cleaning of our housing estates, air conditioner servicing, security, or retail.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most importantly, we must treat everyone with dignity and respect, and value everyone for the work they do.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we join our brothers and sisters in the NTUC to affirm that “Every Worker Matters”.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not just a slogan; it is a fundamental tenet undergirding our entire approach of nation building.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides dealing with inequality, we must ensure that social mobility remains alive and well in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have done better in this aspect than many other advanced economies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But any society which has been stable for a long time tends to stratify.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we must collectively lean against this tendency and do more to uplift disadvantaged groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Here, support in the early years matters critically.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have been making significant shifts on early childhood over the past few years and we will do more to narrow the preschool enrolment gap between children from lower-income households and their peers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also helping lower-income families tackle the complex and multi-faceted challenges they face holistically and through better coordination.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, we have different Government agencies overseeing various schemes – for example, HDB has the Fresh Start Housing Scheme, MOE has its UPLIFT Initiative, and ECDA has KidSTART and so on.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The officers engaging these families take a different approach.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They do not just promote specific Government schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their starting point is the needs of the families – to find out their concerns, and what we can do to support them, such as helping them secure a better job, or ensuring that their children attend school regularly or have a conducive environment to study in.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are seeing many success stories of families being uplifted through this approach.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires much more work and effort on the part of our officers; it also requires us to work closely with social workers and community partners on the ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But ultimately, it is the best way to encourage and empower families to achieve success and to sustain their progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Tackling inequality and sustaining social mobility is really about making our system of meritocracy work well for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, we have long recognised the problems with an “unbridled" and "winner takes all" meritocracy, which Mr Leon Perera spoke about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we set out to achieve a more open and inclusive meritocracy over a decade ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, I am glad that Mr Leon Perera agrees with and supports the Government’s objectives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, Members would have seen the many moves we have made towards these objectives over the years – from the earliest years of life to our efforts in schools and the labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are not done yet, and we are actively working on all fronts to minimise social barriers and encourage mobility, because this is what Singapore has always been about and must continue to be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are pragmatic and we are also realistic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is not about pursuing the latest fashion or fad in policy thinking.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will focus on what works, and what is effective in bringing us closer to our goals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another group that we are focusing on is our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members spoke about this, including Ms Jessica Tan, Mr Yip Hon Weng, Mr Dennis Tan, Mr Sharael Taha, Mr Henry Kwek, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, Ms Tin Pei Ling and Ms Ng Ling Ling.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They covered many areas, including employment, retirement adequacy and care options.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We all know that as our population ages, our healthcare needs and costs will increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The strains on families and caregivers will grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we have been making moves in the Budget in recent years to take better care of our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Besides providing near-term support, we want to help our seniors live healthily and independently for as long as possible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the past five years, we have seen an overall improvement in the employment rate of senior workers and we will continue to push for further improvements working together with our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As part of the refreshed Action Plan for Successful Ageing, we are also stepping up efforts to help our seniors remain socially active in the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And when our seniors retire, we want them to enjoy their silver years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some Members have expressed concerns that the increase in the ceiling will add to business costs and reduce the take-home pay of middle-income workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I understand the concerns, but I also hope Members appreciate that the move will, in fact, benefit workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because they will have more CPF savings, which can be used for healthcare and housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we know that we need to do this over a period of time to give our employers and employees time to adjust.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The annual salary ceiling will also remain unchanged at this juncture, which was also part of the considerations after consultations and this will limit the impact on business costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond the moves in this Budget, we are undertaking a review of our CPF system parameters and retirement policies, including the Silver Support Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our aim is to assure all Singaporeans that as long as they work and contribute consistently to their CPF, they will be able to meet their Basic Retirement Sum.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And for those who do not have the ability to work, or the runway to work and save through CPF, we will find other ways to ensure their retirement security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also looking at the long-term care arrangements for our seniors, something which many Members spoke about.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many are concerned over the affordability of the care options and the burden of care amongst caregivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some have suggested providing more support for caregivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to review, but it is not just about caregiving support alone, because we have to review more broadly our aged care system to see how we can enhance the care and living options for the seniors within our community, while ensuring our long-term care services remain affordable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are looking at various things, including how we can develop more senior living options in our housing estates, how we can best deploy and operate our Active Ageing Centres, something I spoke about in the Budget Statement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And beyond the hardware and infrastructure, how we can provide a more seamless continuum of care for our seniors, with easily accessible and integrated services across all neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is challenging, as the aged care sector is complex and fragmented.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will need to think through our plans carefully and consider how best to deploy limited resources – both land and manpower – in efficient and sensible ways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has always been our approach to providing assurance for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We review our policies carefully, we ensure that any long-term or permanent programmes are sustainable and reinforce the ethos of self-reliance and mutual support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we have progressively strengthened our social security system and safety nets, and implemented schemes like Workfare, CPF LIFE and Silver Support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But as I said in the Budget speech, the moves in this Budget are part of a broader review to strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And many Members gave very good suggestions in this debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ms Yeo Wan Ling talked about how we can better support gig and self-employed workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Dr Wan Rizal, Ms Nadia Samdin and Mr Melvin Yong spoke about those with mental health needs or conditions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Darryl David and Mr Eric Chua spoke about how we can make Singapore more family-friendly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Don Wee, Dr Shahira Abdullah, Ms He Ting Ru, Mr Louis Ng and Ms Rachel Ong have highlighted other groups who need help, including persons with disabilities and their caregivers, students with special needs, healthcare workers and single parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are reviewing all these and many other areas as part of Forward Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the coming months, we will study the various suggestions provided and partner Singaporeans to develop new strategies and impactful solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about looking after our children, grandchildren and future generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must do what is right for today and for tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the earlier decades when our economy took off and grew rapidly, they did not just spend all the surpluses without any regard for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, they painstakingly built up the reserves and they introduced the Elected Presidency to safeguard and protect our reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These values of discipline, prudence and the willingness to sacrifice for the next generation are the very essence of what undergirds our framework for the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking after future generations does not mean that we are neglecting the current generation – far from it.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sometimes, we talk about the future as though it is some distant thing, many years away.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But, in fact, the so-called "future generations" are really not very far away.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many in this Chamber will still be alive 20 or 30 years from now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Prof Koh shared his hopes to be in Singapore in 2050 as a retired professor looking at how green Singapore will be.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I certainly hope to be there at that time too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our children will certainly be growing up in that timeframe and will be directly impacted by what we do today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the future is not something abstract, something that is not linked to us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In any case, all of us today are currently benefiting from the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our reserves are our endowment fund and our rainy-day fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our endowment fund, the returns from our reserves have enabled us to keep overall tax burden light, as I have shown just now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We saw both during the Global Financial Crisis and over the past three years how our reserves helped us to weather crises without having to incur debt that future generations will have to pay.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, what we enjoy today must never be taken for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many Members highlighted this, including Ms Foo Mee Har, Dr Lim Wee Kiak, Ms Poh Li San, Ms Joan Pereira and Mr Shawn Huang.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As they highlighted, we will have to brace ourselves for all sorts of possible disruptions and shocks in this new world and we have to do more to strengthen our national resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had SARS in 2003 and then COVID-19 almost 20 years later in 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We may not need to wait another 20 years before we face the prospect of another deadly and devastating pandemic in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We face global warming and the growing threat of climate-related disasters.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It can facilitate the spread of more illnesses and pandemics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We now have superpower rivalry between China and the US and potential flashpoints in the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The superpowers are now thinking in terms of "spheres of influence".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, smaller countries like Singapore will come under growing pressure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have enjoyed peace and stability in the region for close to 50 years since the end of the Vietnam War.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is hard for us to imagine how things could be different.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But look at Ukraine and Europe and how the situation changed so quickly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With growing geopolitical tensions, can we be sure that our region will be able to avoid conflict in the coming decades?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If there were to be a conflict or a hot war in this part of the world, how will that impact Singapore?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are major risks that we will have to consider and take seriously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And given these plausible scenarios of the future, what should our response be?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To blithely spend more from the reserves as the Opposition proposes because we are just slowing down the growth rate as they claim?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Or to husband our reserves and uphold the principles that underpin the protection of our reserves that have served us well all these years?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In fact, I would say that there appeared to be a time when the Workers' Party seemed to me, to share the Government's perspective on the reserves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He said, and I quote, "Past Reserves are a strategic asset meant for use in times of need, especially when the Government faces financial constraints due to unprecedented circumstances which require the Government to respond in the interest of the nation." I could not have said it better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Later in 2011, after we recovered well from the crisis, we were able to put back into Past Reserves what we had drawn earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He said in his speech in Parliament that this was "one thing right" that the Government had done in the Budget that year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several PAP Members of Parliament – Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim and Ms Tin Pei Ling – have over this and recent Budgets emphasised the importance of fiscal discipline and urged the Government to try to put back the money into the Past Reserves should our fiscal position improve.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the Workers' Party has been completely silent on this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Different options and different suggestions dressed up in multiple ways but it boils down to the same consistent ask.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it sounds to me that the Workers' Party has shifted its position since the days of Mr Low.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in the end, Singaporeans will have to judge what is the more responsible approach to manage our finances and to take Singapore forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I say, let us uphold the values of our forefathers and do what is right by past, present and future generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us maintain a strong fiscal foundation so that Singapore can continue to prosper and thrive for many more years to come in this troubled world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To conclude, Mr Deputy Speaker, the Budget is not just about dollars and cents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Neither is it about winners and losers or about pitting the well off against the rest of society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, it reflects our values as a people and our unwavering commitment to build a fairer, more inclusive and ever more just society.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In his opening remarks, Mr Pritam Singh gave an impassioned speech – that we must not allow "two Singapores" to emerge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This has in fact been the People's Action Party Government's steadfast approach all these years, so I thank him for agreeing with what we are doing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But I must say that I find it a bit odd how Mr Pritam Singh characterises the "two Singapores".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In particular, he suggested that if you are unable to upgrade to a condominium or a landed property or own a car, you will be in the second Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the test of social mobility cannot be about owning a landed property or purchasing a car.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Let us not perpetuate such narrow definitions of success.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The fact is everyone will have their own aspirations and passions to pursue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, we aim to value and celebrate every individual for who they are and to provide them with opportunities to do better throughout their lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we will refresh and strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And I cannot help but feel that it is because the Workers' Party thinks that there is political mileage, perhaps, in pushing for ideas to soak the rich and, maybe, political advantage to reject the GST despite everything we have done to implement it in a way that is fair and that does not hurt the poor.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is what the PAP Government and successive People's Action Party Ministers for Finance have done.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the end, I have faith in Singapore and Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We know what it means to live within our means, earn our own keep and stand on our own feet with dignity and pride.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We care about our children and grandchildren and our future generations yet to be born.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have kept Singapore going through good years and bad.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I have a number of clarifications in view of the interventions the Finance Minister made on the Workers' Party's participation in this debate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I will start with the first and this pertains to the tax burden on the middle class.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the Finance Minister put up some charts.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: They set out what the Government has shared in the past about the burden insofar as how much a certain percentile of Singaporeans pay vis-a-vis taxes and the benefits they accrue in return.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think this has been something that the Government has done consistently.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Government would say it would do this when it was ready.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think we saw the headlines this morning about CPI and how it continues to go up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I am raising this now vis-a-vis those charts that the Finance Minister provided because you have to assess the pain points of the middle class from various perspectives.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I think the CPI, when you look at certain specific categories and classes of Singaporeans, you may get a different picture compared to what the Finance Minister raised.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: We obviously need a better resolution on that.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My first clarification is whether the Finance Minister would consider providing information from that perspective – specific groups of Singaporeans which we know are in the sandwiched middle class.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second clarification has to deal with the strategy that the Finance Minister laid out.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Government keeps the tax burden low and it aims to keep the tax burden on Singaporeans low.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: In the course of the debate, of course, I listened to various PAP Members of Parliament (MPs).

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I heard proposals for more intermediate- and long-term care subsidies, checking the rental rate of Government-owned and managed properties, even a call for a windfall tax.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Many of these proposals were made in the WP manifesto and by WP Members in this House.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, for a minute, I thought that the PAP had become "WP-lite".

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Be that as it may, what none of the PAP MPs who raised these proposals did, was to tell us where this money was going to come from, something that the WP did in the last debate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The Finance Minister referred to the debate we had at the last Budget debate.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: What then are the main strategies then that the Government has for keeping the tax burden on Singaporeans low?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: This leads me to my third clarification and that pertains to the Housing and Development Board (HDB) issue.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: I will be brief on this because I am sure some of the other WP MPs will come in and seek further clarifications from the Finance Minister.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: On this topic and the Minister's iteration of this back and forth that is currently going on in The Straits Times Forum between the PAP and the WP, I am reminded of what the Government Whip said many, many years ago in this House, "Sometimes it is not just what you say but what you do not say that also matters." And what the Government is not saying, of course, is the context of the WP housing paper was in response to Voluntary Early Redevelopment Scheme (VERS), a Government proposal which was not very clear and it was looking into the future.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, naturally, the housing paper looks at a longer-range forecast of the housing sector.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And that was the context which I have not heard any PAP MP speak about.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And in fact, they seem to be quite silent about it.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And, on this note, of course, I have to then come to the irresistible conclusion that it is a convenient distraction because if indeed the point that was raised in the housing paper was critical, then the PAP would have raised it last year when the WP called for more HDB housing for singles.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, it was a response to the housing debate, I think the PAP recognised that accessibility and affordability of HDB flats is a serious issue, but I will leave it at that on the point of context.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The second sub-point, however, I would like to make is an issue that the Finance Minister suggested that we do not want to deal with the difficult problem of subsidies and grants and how much this may cost the taxpayer.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: Completely untrue, because we raised it in this House.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: And given the approach that we are taking, this is only going to increase.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: So, when the Finance Minister says, when we ask questions about pricing of land and so forth, and he says that this is red herring, I respectfully disagree because we have to try and understand how we can make the Budget balanced, and how much is actually being devoted for a programme which the way we see it is just going to keep going up and up and up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: The other WP MPs will come in with more clarifications.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
text: My fourth point has to do with —

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Singh, may I invite you to be more succinct in your clarifications because we would have to go through quite a number of Members seeking clarifications of the Minister for Finance.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: If you can keep it succinct, it would be appreciated.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The fourth clarification is pertaining to the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) which the Finance Minister did pick up.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The Finance Minister shared that overall, there was good progress.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I raised this point in my Budget speech last year as well.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Can the Finance Minister share some of this information with us?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I think we do need a report card.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The final clarification pertains to the point the Finance Minister made about Mr Low and his responses to the drawdown of the reserves during the Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The simple answer to that is the position of the Workers' Party has evolved because circumstances have evolved significantly.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: And we can see it also, in terms of the contribution of the NIRC and the Government's own attitude to the NII framework post-Global Financial Crisis.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: These are perfectly, eminently reasonable explanations as to why Temasek tap was included in the NIRC framework.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I do not see this as a particularly problematic issue to deal with because naturally, as circumstances evolve, PAP also will change its position and the Workers' Party, of course, will be entitled to do the same.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: I will leave those clarifications out there for the moment and I will step in with more if I have to.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the tax burden on different, middle-income and sandwiched groups and the CPI for these specific segments, we do the best we can.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We continue to monitor all the different groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Where data is available, we will publish and where it is useful, we will put it out for information.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are tracking not only inflation, but as we have repeatedly said, how real incomes evolve for all these different segments, because at the end of the day, we want to ensure that real incomes grow not just for the top end, but for the middle and, in particular and especially for the lower-income groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We, already, in fact, put out CPI data by income groups.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Leader of the Opposition has asked for even more granular data for specific segments, different archetypes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to review and see what more can be done.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are all concerned about the same thing and we will continue to do more and do better.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the strategy for keeping tax burden low and who has given more ideas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In this House, Members across different parties will put out ideas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: From the Government's point of view, we welcome all ideas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Where they are good ideas, regardless of where these ideas come from, we embrace them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If the ideas may not be so effective, we will highlight and say that these are not ideas that we think are sound.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And here, my appeal to everyone in the House, everyone in the House, across all parties is, as Finance Minister, you hear a lot more proposals to do more, but you very rarely hear proposals to stop doing something.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think it would be nice for a change to hear Members talk about some things we might stop doing, do less of.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And then, we may have more ideas to think about how we can manage both expenditure and revenues, and ensure sustainable finances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Third, on housing and what the Workers' Party said in its Working Paper in 2019 and the context which, according to Mr Singh was not said.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Actually, I thought I said it in the speech.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I fully appreciate the context, because I was there in the Ministry of National Development (MND).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The context was the concern about decay of leases, declining values.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the context was also in the midst of falling resale prices for consecutive years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the Workers' Party is not alone in highlighting that, under such an environment, we better consider how many new flats we are putting out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I was under tremendous pressure to cut back BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is no shame in acknowledging that you got that wrong because many people did.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Why not just acknowledge it, that, yes, it may not have been a specific proposal or whatever you want to call it, but it was very clearly stated.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not have to go through it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I read the Working Paper, from cover to cover, in MND.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And what was said at that time reflected the context of that time – a concern with overhang of supply, too many flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you build more flats, this is what will happen.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, why not just acknowledge that you got that wrong?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many experts thought it was the right thing to do at that time too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are not here to pass judgement because, with the benefit of hindsight it is, of course, very easy to say.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: No one would have predicted that you would have a COVID-19 crisis and what has happened in the last three years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We did not; neither did the Workers' Party.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, let us acknowledge, like I said, with some humility, what happened, and let us not rush to judge the current situation with the benefit of hindsight.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us acknowledge that the current situation was created by a set of very unusual and exceptional circumstances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And the root of the problem is building more supply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are doing our best to try and fix the problem – not created by bad policies, by sacred cows which we are loath to slay, but by something that was exceptional.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And we are doing our best to address it.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Fourthly, ITMs and what was said in the Estimates Committee about robust KPI setting, outcomes and publishing of what we have achieved through the ITMs.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We need clear KPIs, outcomes for every ITM and they had been published, not all, but a lot of them have very clear outcomes reported.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the financial services sector which I launched, for example, we set out very clearly what we wanted to deliver, what was achieved and the next milestone, what we hope to do with the next version.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sector-by-sector, these ITMs, the sectoral agencies in charge of them, will put out the reports, more information, clearer outcomes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a continuing journey which we will continue to walk on and help each sector restructure and transform.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More importantly, our underlying philosophy, our intent, our principles, have never changed and will never change.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I wish to respond to the point in the HDB paper and then I have two clarifications to put to the Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And to some extent time, I am repeating what Mr Louis Chua said on the point about the HDB paper when it was first made, but I think it needs some treatment in a bit more granularity than what the Leader of the Opposition had time to do just now.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Because the People's Action Party seems to be doubling down on this incorrect assertion, using its tremendous PR and communicative machinery to repeat this assertion about the Workers’ Party HDB paper again and again, on social media, in letters to The Straits Times, Zaobao.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, let me go back to that and we can read out those two paragraphs.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I am glad the Deputy Prime Minister read our paper.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The first paragraph makes observations about the risk of vacancies in the context of a paper on longer-term housing dynamics; that resale prices will inevitably come under pressure at some point.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And I think the Government has acknowledged that.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: I refer to the exchange between Senior Minister of State Sim Ann and Assoc Prof Jamus Lim, my colleague.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It does not say BTO projects should continue at a reduced rate; it does not say BTO projects should stop.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It does not say BTO projects should continue but at 9,000 rather than 17,000.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It says, BTO projects should continue and then it goes on to say that you can taper that down in the longer term when our USB proposal kicks in, which would yield flats that could be repurposed as Sale of Balance flats (SBF) or for expanded public rental scheme.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: But that only starts to kick in in about 12 years’ time.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, I think it is very important to have debates on our real positions and not mischaracterise one another's positions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: We did not put out a proposal in 2019 that you cut BTO construction.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: If we had wanted to, we would have set that out clearly in plain language.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: My other two clarifications to the Deputy Prime Minister.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Mr Perera, if I could ask you to keep them short and concise.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Deputy Prime Minister asked, why does Workers' Party say a HPI of three, why not a HPI of two or lower?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: There is an organisation called Demographia and the Government in its Parliamentary Question (PQ) replies have referred to the research of this particular organisation.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: I do not think the Government would have done that if it is not an organisation that does not do credible work.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, there is some basis in the research and the science around this to say that that figure of three is a good affordability target.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, I would like to ask the Deputy Prime Minister for what the People's Action Party seems to be saying, that anything below five is fine.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: And the last clarification, I will keep it brief – in response to the Leader of the Opposition, the Deputy Prime Minister has set out a worldview that reducing the rate of growth of reserves is taking away from past generations.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: In 2008, the PAP did just that – when it created the Net Investments Return (NIR) Framework, slowed it even more, in 2015 with adding Temasek.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: So, why is that not irresponsible and not taking money away from future generations?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: But when the Workers’ Party says it, then is irresponsible!

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is it seeking political mileage that it is okay when you do it but it is not okay when we call for it?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: First, on the housing Working Paper and what the Workers’ Party said.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think, Mr Perera now is sort of alluding to the fact that the assessment that they had put out was pertaining more to a longer-term concern about a supply overhang.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But that is very clearly not what the write-up says.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There was a concern about short-term overhang; in the short term, too many supply of new flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not just you who was highlighting this concern.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I probably think some PAP MPs must have asked me the same question.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I was under a lot of pressure to cut back BTO new flats, the building of new flats –precisely because of the short-term concern.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It was very clear what was written; and arising from this assessment therefore, that there was the concern that you have to calibrate your building programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To me, as somebody who was looking at the Working Paper then, on the receiving end in MND, I think it was as clear as daylight what the Workers’ Party wanted to do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, all we are highlighting is let us be upfront and honest that the assessment made at that time was not right.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Like I said, many people did not get it right.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: No one would have predicted what happened with COVID-19, but there is no shame in that.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us now focus, look forward on coming together to tackle what the root cause of the problem is, which is what the PAP Government is indeed doing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On affordability benchmarks, yes, there are a range of benchmarks out there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We do not deny that, but we have made clear what the affordability benchmarks are.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our pricing of new flats have not changed at all these years from then till now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have put all of that out.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I can appreciate why anyone looking at it from an opposition point of view will say, "well, that is very good but let us make it cheaper, let us make it more affordable".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And obviously, in this current time when the resale prices are high, whatever you say on that front will have more traction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: People will feel the pain and they will say "yes, of course cheaper is better".

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But remember, at the time when prices came down, this was not so much of an issue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, all I am highlighting is let us have some perspective on this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The market moves up and down in cycles.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Let us understand the root cause of what causes the cycles and let us continue with a certain consistency in policy and address the root cause of the problem.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Then, on the NIR framework and why if the PAP Government were to make a change, it is okay; but if the Workers’ Party were to propose something, we say it is not okay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think we have been through this debate too in this House.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I have explained, from the Government's point of view, we put in place a framework, we staged out the implementation over a period of time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We always had the intention for Temasek to be there but we put in place a framework that will provide discipline for the Government to use the reserves as an endowment fund.
